messages:
Alex M.: heads-up — i'm planning a small refactor to consolidate the 'query graph' plumbing that panels use. want to align on RBAC handshake, caching, and fallback behavior before we land anything. pinging @Priya K. @Jordan T. for perf + auth tradeoffs.
Priya K.: SGTM. my main worry is the extra hop + auth per subquery. naive approach adds ~5–15ms p99. do we batch auth calls or centralize admission?
Jordan T.: batching helps but increases coupling. alternative: per-session capability token cached at the adapter layer; sign with short TTL. avoids auth fanout but needs cache invalidation on permission change.
Samira N.: +1 on adapter layer. prefer async prefetch of capability tokens during panel init, then use local cache for subsequent slices. keeps panel wire protocol stable.
Luca R.: ran a quick prototype: adapter + local token cache -> 2x throughput under synthetic load, but memory climbed ~10% due to per-session KV entries. logs: `adapter:cache:entries=1200 mem_rss=1.1G` (attached in staging).
Alex M.: memory bump acceptable if we can bound growth. what's the rollback plan if cache causes OOMs?
Priya K.: we should have a conservative eviction policy (LRU with max-entries) and an admin evict endpoint. tokens TTL should be short (60s) and we must emit audit events on evict/refresh.
Jordan T.: another tradeoff: batching reduces auth calls but complicates partial fanout when a panel needs many small slices. hybrid heuristic: if slice_count > 8 then batch, else single token flow. keeps tail latency predictable.
Samira N.: implementation sketch: 
```yaml
adapter:
  auth_cache_ttl_seconds: 60
  max_cache_entries: 5000
  batch_auth_threshold: 8
  evict_endpoint: /admin/evict-token
```
we can wire config flags for canary.
Luca R.: for perf validation i'll add a benchmark that simulates 200 qps with 50ms backend latency and 30 panels concurrently. will post numbers in #eng-performance.
Alex M.: plan sounds good. steps: 1) adapter + config flags, 2) add admin evict + audit logging, 3) perf tests + mem guard, 4) canary 10% tenants, 5) full cutover. i'll open a short RFC follow-up with the checklist.
Priya K.: one more: ensure the adapter attaches a `x-tenant-perm-version` header so downstream can short-circuit cached decisions when perms change.
Jordan T.: agree. also recommend a metrics slice: auth_cache_hit, auth_cache_miss, auth_evicts, auth_refresh_latency.
Samira N.: i'll draft the runbook for rollback and include the admin evict commands.
DevOps-Bot: deploy triggered: staging/adapter v0.3.1 -> started (build #4521).
Alex M.: thanks everyone :thumbsup: i'll kick off the RFC update and assign owners for the perf test and runbook.
